study_label: PAST-BP intensive versus standard blood-pressure targets after stroke/TIA

objective.value: To determine whether setting a more intensive blood-pressure target in primary care after stroke or TIA would lead to lower blood pressure, as a prelude to a trial assessing stroke recurrence.

population.value: Patients on general-practice TIA/stroke registers, recruited from practices in England during 2009-11. Exclusions included baseline systolic blood pressure below 125 mm Hg, use of three or more antihypertensive agents, postural systolic change greater than 20 mm Hg, existing treatment to a 130 mm Hg target, inability to consent, or insufficient evidence of prior stroke/TIA.

intervention.value: Intensive systolic blood-pressure target: below 130 mm Hg, or a 10 mm Hg reduction for patients with baseline systolic blood pressure 125-140 mm Hg. Blood-pressure management used practice-nurse monitoring and general-practitioner treatment modification.

comparator.value: Standard systolic blood-pressure target of below 140 mm Hg irrespective of baseline blood pressure, with otherwise identical blood-pressure management.

duration_follow_up.value: One-year follow-up; blood pressure was measured at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months.

primary_outcome.value: Change in systolic blood pressure between baseline and one year.

effect_result.value: At 12 months, the intensive target was associated with a significantly greater reduction in systolic blood pressure: systolic blood pressure was reduced by 16 mm Hg in the intensive-target arm and 13 mm Hg in the standard-target arm. Sensitivity calculations reported between-group differences of -3.2 mm Hg (95% CI -5.8 to -0.64) using the fifth and sixth readings and -3.3 mm Hg (95% CI -5.8 to -0.67) using the second through sixth readings.

safety.value: At 12 months, the most common symptoms showed no significant differences between groups.

sample_size.analyzed: 379 with primary-outcome data at 1 year (182 intensive-target; 197 standard-target)
sample_size.display: 529 randomized; 379 analyzed for the primary outcome at 1 year; 610 planned
